data.description:
## Description

**What**: Update REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md and dispatch.py to dispatch cycle-N+1 reviews as two structurally independent calls. Call 1: diff + structured prior_findings_index (IDs + cited_lines + dimension only — no defense_text). Call 2: receives Call 1 output + full prior_findings.json + defenses[]. Reviewer self-declares relation per finding in Call 2.
**Why**: SC1 statefulness substrate. Two-call architecture replaces the in-prompt sequential gate that does not work through transformer attention (bot-psychologist critical finding).
**Scope**:
  IN:
  - First-cycle reviews remain single-call; cycle N>=2 uses two calls
  - Call 2 receives Call 1's findings JSON and adds relation field
  - Orchestrator wires both calls in /dso:review and CI dispatch.py identically
  - STATEFUL_REVIEW_CONTEXT block is conditionally injected; first-cycle reviewer prompts unchanged
  OUT:
  - Single-call first-cycle reviews
  - Orchestrator overlap verification (S9)
  - Arbiter dispatch (S10)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, cycle-N+1 reviews execute as two litellm/Agent calls, with Call 1 seeing only the prior_findings_index and Call 2 receiving full defenses[] before assigning relation fields
  ← Satisfies: "Stateful re-review with two-call reviewer architecture, orchestrator-side proximity-overlap verification, and severity-history telemetry"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Performance] Doubles cycle-N+1 latency vs single-call; acceptable trade-off for structural independence
- [Testing] Test fixtures verify Call 1 receives only the prior_findings_index, not defense_text

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a cycle-N+1 reviewer, I run as a two-call architecture (Call 1 diff-only with prior_findings_index; Call 2 with full prior_findings + defenses)
